title: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
summary: Gavrilo Princip, a Bosnian Serb nationalist, shoots the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne. Within six weeks the great powers are at war.

title: First Battle of the Marne
summary: After the German army overruns much of northern France and Belgium, the French and British halt their retreat on the Marne and drive the Germans back, ending the German plan to win the war quickly by taking Paris.

title: Gallipoli landings
summary: Allied troops, including Australians and New Zealanders, land to try to knock the Ottomans out of the war. They are held by forces including Mustafa Kemal and withdraw after eight months.

title: Armenian genocide
summary: The Ottoman government organises the deportation and mass killing of around a million Armenians, as well as Assyrians and Greeks.

title: Battle of the Somme
summary: British and French armies attack German lines on the river Somme. On the first day the British suffer 57,470 casualties, the worst in their army's history; by November more than a million men have been killed or wounded.

title: October Revolution
summary: Lenin's Bolsheviks seize power in Petrograd. After a civil war they found the Soviet Union (1922), the first communist state.

title: Armistice ends the First World War
summary: Fighting stops at 11 a.m. on 11 November. About 17 million people have died, and the German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman empires collapse.

title: 1918 influenza pandemic
summary: A flu pandemic infects about a third of the world's population and kills an estimated 25–50 million people — more than the war.

title: Treaty of Versailles
summary: The peace imposed on Germany redraws Europe's map and creates the League of Nations; its harsh terms fuel German resentment.

title: Republic of Turkey founded
summary: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk proclaims the republic after the Turkish War of Independence; the Ottoman sultanate and caliphate are abolished.

sources.title: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey

title: Mussolini's March on Rome
summary: Fascist blackshirts converge on Rome and the king appoints Benito Mussolini prime minister; he soon makes himself dictator.

title: Fleming discovers penicillin
summary: The Scottish physician Alexander Fleming discovers penicillin, one of the first medicines effective against many bacterial infections. Mass-produced from 1943, it greatly reduced deaths from infected wounds among Allied forces in the Second World War.

title: Wall Street Crash
summary: Black Tuesday: the US stock market collapses, triggering the Great Depression worldwide.

title: Gandhi's Salt March
summary: Mahatma Gandhi leads a 24-day march to Dandi to make salt in protest against the British salt monopoly. His breaking of the salt laws sparks civil disobedience by millions of Indians.

title: Hitler becomes Chancellor
summary: Adolf Hitler is appointed Chancellor of Germany and within months turns it into a Nazi dictatorship.

title: The Long March
summary: Encircled by Nationalist forces, the Chinese Communists retreat some 10,000 km; Mao Zedong emerges as their leader.

title: Nanjing Massacre
summary: During the Second Sino-Japanese War, Japanese troops murder and rape huge numbers of civilians and prisoners after capturing Nanjing.

title: Germany invades Poland
summary: Germany invades Poland; Britain and France declare war two days later. The Soviet Union invades from the east on 17 September. The Second World War begins in Europe.

title: Battle of Britain
summary: The RAF defeats the Luftwaffe's attempt to win air superiority, forcing Hitler to call off his invasion of Britain.

title: Operation Barbarossa
summary: Germany and its allies invade the Soviet Union with over three million troops — the largest invasion in history. The Holocaust escalates behind the front.

title: Attack on Pearl Harbor
summary: Japan's surprise attack on the US Pacific Fleet brings the United States into the war.

title: Battle of Stalingrad
summary: One of the bloodiest battles in history. The encirclement and surrender of the German Sixth Army in February 1943 marks the turning point of the war in Europe.

title: Battle of Midway
summary: US carrier aircraft sink four Japanese carriers, turning the tide of the Pacific War.

title: The Holocaust: Auschwitz-Birkenau
summary: Nazi Germany systematically murders six million Jews, along with Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners and others. About 1.1 million people are killed at Auschwitz alone.

title: D-Day: Normandy landings
summary: The largest seaborne invasion in history lands about 156,000 Allied soldiers in Normandy, beginning the liberation of France and Western Europe.

title: Germany surrenders (V-E Day)
summary: A week after Hitler's suicide, Germany surrenders unconditionally. The war in Europe is over.

title: Atomic bombing of Hiroshima
summary: The United States drops an atomic bomb on Hiroshima, then on Nagasaki three days later, killing well over 100,000 people. Japan surrenders on 15 August.

sources.title: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

title: United Nations founded
summary: The UN Charter comes into force, creating an organisation to maintain international peace.

title: Independence and Partition of India
summary: British India becomes independent as two states, India and Pakistan. Partition causes the migration of some 15 million people and up to a million deaths.

title: State of Israel founded
summary: David Ben-Gurion declares Israel's independence; neighbouring Arab states invade. Around 700,000 Palestinian Arabs flee or are expelled (the Nakba).

title: People's Republic of China proclaimed
summary: Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic after the Communists win the civil war; the Nationalists retreat to Taiwan.

sources.title: Proclamation of the People's Republic of China

title: Korean War
summary: North Korea invades the South; UN forces led by the US and Chinese armies join in. The armistice of 1953 leaves Korea divided at the 38th parallel.

title: Structure of DNA described
summary: Watson and Crick, using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray images, publish the double-helix structure of DNA.

title: Ghana becomes independent
summary: Under Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana is the first sub-Saharan colony to win independence; 17 African nations follow in 1960 alone.

title: Sputnik 1
summary: The Soviet Union launches the first artificial satellite, starting the Space Race.

title: Cuban Revolution
summary: Fidel Castro's guerrillas overthrow the dictator Batista.

title: Yuri Gagarin, first human in space
summary: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbits the Earth once in Vostok 1.

title: Berlin Wall built
summary: East Germany seals off West Berlin with barbed wire, then a concrete wall — the symbol of the Cold War's 'Iron Curtain'.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis
summary: Thirteen days in which the US and USSR come closer to nuclear war than ever before, over Soviet missiles in Cuba.

title: 'I Have a Dream'
summary: Martin Luther King Jr. speaks to 250,000 people at the March on Washington; the Civil Rights Act follows in 1964.

title: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
summary: President Kennedy is shot while riding in a motorcade through Dallas.

title: Cultural Revolution
summary: Mao launches a campaign to purge 'bourgeois' elements; Red Guards persecute millions and the country is thrown into chaos for a decade.

title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
summary: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walk on the Moon: 'one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind'.

title: First ARPANET message
summary: The first message is sent between computers at UCLA and Stanford over ARPANET, the ancestor of the internet. (The system crashed after 'LO'.)

title: Fall of Saigon
summary: North Vietnamese forces take Saigon, ending the Vietnam War; the country is reunified under communist rule.

title: Iranian Revolution
summary: The Shah is overthrown and Ayatollah Khomeini establishes an Islamic Republic.

title: China's 'Reform and Opening Up'
summary: Deng Xiaoping launches market reforms; special economic zones like Shenzhen begin China's transformation into the world's factory.

title: Chernobyl disaster
summary: A reactor explodes at the Chernobyl nuclear plant, spreading radioactive fallout across Europe.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: East German border guards open the crossings and Berliners begin tearing down the Wall. Communist regimes across Eastern Europe fall within months.

title: Tiananmen Square crackdown
summary: The Chinese army crushes student-led pro-democracy protests in Beijing, killing hundreds or more.

title: The World Wide Web goes public
summary: Tim Berners-Lee, a scientist at CERN, publishes the first website and opens the Web to everyone.

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
summary: Gorbachev resigns and the Soviet flag is lowered over the Kremlin; the USSR splits into 15 independent states. The Cold War is over.

title: Nelson Mandela becomes President
summary: After 27 years in prison, Mandela is inaugurated as South Africa's first Black president following the end of apartheid.

title: Rwandan genocide
summary: Over about 100 days, Hutu militias systematically kill members of the Tutsi minority, as well as some moderate Hutu and Twa. Most scholarly estimates put the number of Tutsi killed at between 500,000 and 662,000.

title: The euro is launched
summary: Eleven EU countries adopt a common currency; notes and coins arrive in 2002.

title: September 11 attacks
summary: Al-Qaeda terrorists hijack four airliners and kill nearly 3,000 people. The US invades Afghanistan and, in 2003, Iraq.

title: Indian Ocean tsunami
summary: A magnitude 9.2–9.3 earthquake off Sumatra causes a tsunami that kills an estimated 227,898 people in 14 countries, the deadliest tsunami in history.

title: The smartphone era: iPhone unveiled
summary: Apple announces the iPhone, a smartphone with a multi-touch screen and almost no physical buttons. It quickly becomes Apple's most successful product and transforms the smartphone industry.

title: Global financial crisis
summary: Lehman Brothers collapses, setting off the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

title: Arab Spring
summary: Protests topple Tunisia's president and spread to Egypt, Libya, Syria, Yemen and beyond; Syria descends into civil war.

title: Paris Climate Agreement
summary: Nearly every nation agrees to limit global warming to well below 2 °C above pre-industrial levels.

title: COVID-19 declared a pandemic
summary: A new coronavirus spreads worldwide; lockdowns affect billions of people and the pandemic kills millions.

title: Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine
summary: Russia launches the largest attack on a European state since 1945; Ukraine resists, and the war becomes a long war of attrition.

title: Generative AI goes mainstream
summary: The release of ChatGPT brings large language models to hundreds of millions of people within months, setting off a global race in artificial intelligence.
